Subject: Audit logs and data access evidence - post-call recap

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of FinCo Bank's use cases. Quick recap from our discovery and agreed next steps: 

- Scope: you want an audit trail of who accessed model inference/data (who/what/when) for regulatory reporting and internal investigations.
- Key controls you flagged: user identity preservation, IP/geo, action type (query/export/admin), retention window, and exportability for subpoenas/audits.
- Residency: primary concern is EU data residency for production traffic and the ability to store audit logs in customer-controlled locations for Private/Dedicated.

Next steps I mentioned on the call:
1) I will share a sample audit logs export (CSV) showing typical columns and redaction behavior.
2) Marissa (solutions engineering) will provide a short note on retention defaults and options across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
3) We’ll confirm whether SOC 2 artifacts and DPA countersign are available for your procurement team.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the team through the sample and export process (propose Thurs 3/26).

If anything above is missing or misstated, let me know. I’ll send the sample export & retention doc in a follow-up email — looping Marissa and Ben for any technical or contract questions.

Best,

Thanks Alex — that summary is accurate. A few follow-ups / clarifications from our end before the follow-up call: 

- Export format: preferred CSV or Parquet; can you confirm whether exports include a raw request payload or only metadata? We need to ensure PII (customer names, account numbers) are not present in exported logs by default.
- Fields: please confirm the set of fields available (timestamp, user_id/email, action, resource, ip, request_id, any session id). Is the requestor identity always an email or can it be an internal service account id?
- Retention: what is the default retention window for hosted vs dedicated? Can retention be set by customer to 90/180/365 days?
- Residency: can audit logs be stored in an EU region only (we are proceeding under EU data residency requirements for production)?
- Evidence: procurement needs a sample CSV, a redlineable DPA, and SOC 2 Type II summary (or specific artifact showing access controls). What is your expected turnaround on those?

We'd like the sample CSV ahead of the call if possible. Also looping procurement (Tom) on timelines.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Senior PM, Security & Compliance
FinCo Bank

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@fincobank.com>, Tom Herrera <t.herrera@fincobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logs and data access evidence - post-call recap

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the items we discussed: audit-logs-sample.csv and redwood-data-retention.pdf. I’ve also attached the DPA template (docusign-data-processing-agreement.pdf) for procurement to review.

Short answers up front, details below:
- Export formats: CSV, JSON, and Parquet are supported. Attached sample is a trimmed CSV (columns described below).
- What’s included: exports contain metadata about requests, not full prompt text by default for Hosted accounts. Columns in the sample: 
  timestamp
  request_id
  user_email
  actor_type
  action
  resource
  ip_address
  region
  model_version
  response_size_tokens
  request_hash (SHA256 of request payload; non-reversible)
  export_tooling_notes

- PII: we do NOT include full request/response content in audit exports by default. For teams that opt into longer-term prompt logging (opt-in for Redbox Hosted), we provide controls and explicit consent flows; otherwise we only store hashed request fingerprints and metadata. If you require redaction of specific fields, Marissa can propose a pipeline to filter or redact prior to export.
- Identity: user identity is populated when requests are authenticated. Values may be an email (recommended) or a service account id (svc-xxx). We include both actor_type and user_email columns so you can distinguish human vs service calls.
- Retention: default hosted retention is 30 days for audit metadata; Dedicated and Private deployments support custom retention policies (can configure 90/180/365+ days). See attached redwood-data-retention.pdf for policy matrix.
- Residency: for Dedicated/Private we can keep audit logs in an EU region only; Hosted customers with EU residency requirement are colocated to EU regions and logs remain in-region. Marissa can confirm specific region endpoints for EU.
- Evidence / SOC2: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II summary report and a SOC control matrix within 5 business days; for full SOC binders there’s a standard procurement process. DPA template attached — happy to take redlines.

How exports work (UI/API):
- UI: Admins can select time range and download CSV/JSON/Parquet via Admin Console (single-click).
- API: /v1/admin/audit-exports with time range, format, and optional filters (user_email, action, model_version). API export job returns a presigned URL.
- Typical export size and timing: small ranges (1 day) return in <30s; large ranges (months) are delivered as chunked Parquet within minutes depending on size.

Next step: Marissa, can you add a short technical note on how to configure retention and region for FinCo Bank (Dedicated vs Hosted), and confirm the exact EU endpoints? Also Ben, our legal lead, I’m adding you for DPA and procurement questions.

Sara / Tom — can we lock a 30-min follow-up on Thu 3/26 at 11:00 PT to walk the sample and export UI/API? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193
